title: Costumes then and now, and how long they take
summary: Older costumes were simpler, with turkey feathers; makers dismantle costumes after St. Joseph's Night and start anew.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What were the costumes like when you... We described a costume many years ago. As you said, they're intricate today.

Well, they were much simpler. They were always beautiful. But they seemed to be simpler. They used turkey feathers instead of ostrich plumes. And I don't think they had as much beadwork on them. Now, I don't remember well enough to really discuss them. They were always beautiful, as I recall, but quite a bit simpler.
How long did they work on these costumes?

They usually start working on their costume shortly after St. Joseph's Night, in which they take the costume completely apart and salvage what they can in the way of the sequins and the beads and the plumes, and then start making another costume.

And, of course, they probably don't work as hard, but right now, you can, with Mardi Gras in the early part of February, I think just about all of these fellas are up till midnight working on their costumes from now on in.
